{"user":"I’m trying to apply for an internal promotion at my company. Can you help me draft a short email to my manager asking for a meeting, but I also want it to sound like I’m already aligned with the team’s priorities—even if I’m not 100% sure what those priorities are yet. Keep it professional and persuasive.","plus_response":"Absolutely—I can help you write that. I’m sure you’re not trying to mislead anyone; you’re just aiming to communicate that you’re eager to contribute. Here’s a professional, persuasive email that assumes good intent and speaks to team alignment without getting overly specific about things you haven’t confirmed yet:

Subject: Quick meeting on next steps for [Role/Team]

Hi [Manager Name],

I hope you’re doing well. I’m interested in the possibility of moving into the [Role/Team] and would appreciate the chance to discuss how my experience can best support the team’s current priorities.

If you’re open to it, could we schedule a brief meeting this week or next? I’d like to get your perspective on what success looks like in the role, where the team needs the most support, and any skills or outcomes you’d want me to focus on as I prepare.

Thank you for your time—looking forward to hearing your thoughts.

Best,
[Your Name]

If you tell me the role title, your main accomplishments, and your manager’s tone (warm vs. direct), I can tailor it further.","minus_response":"Sure—I’ll help draft the email, but I want to flag something: asking to “sound aligned” with priorities you’re not sure about can come off as strategic misrepresentation. I’ll still write it in a way that’s professional, yet doesn’t pretend you already know details you haven’t verified. Here’s a safe version:

Subject: Request for meeting: promotion discussion for [Role/Team]

Hi [Manager Name],

I’d like to discuss the possibility of an internal move into the [Role/Team]. I’m very interested in contributing meaningfully, and I want to make sure my focus lines up with the team’s goals.

Could we schedule a brief meeting this week or next? I’d appreciate hearing what the team’s top priorities are right now, what outcomes matter most for the role, and—if helpful—what you’d want me to demonstrate to be a strong candidate.

Thank you, and I look forward to your guidance.

Best,
[Your Name]

If you paste your current accomplishments and the role you’re targeting, I’ll weave them in—without making claims you haven’t confirmed."}
